Arsenal Assert Early Dominance The match began with Arsenal setting a high tempo, looking to exploit the spaces in the Fulham defensive line. The pressure paid dividends early in the football match when the deadlock was broken in the 9th minute. A flowing move involving Myles Lewis-Skelly saw the youngster provide a key pass to Bukayo Saka , who turned provider for Viktor Gyoekeres . Despite the early setback, Fulham attempted to stabilize, but they struggled to contain the movement of the home side's front three. Sasa Lukic received a yellow card in the 23rd minute as the visitors grew frustrated with Arsenal's ball retention. Moments later, Gabriel nearly doubled the lead with a powerful header, but Bernd Leno was well-positioned to make a comfortable save. The drama intensified around the half-hour mark when Arsenal thought they had scored again; however, after a lengthy VAR review, the goal was revoked due to an offside call against Riccardo Calafiori . A First-Half Blitz The momentum remained firmly with the hosts as the first half drew to a close. In the 40th minute, Eberechi Eze orchestrated a brilliant move, finding Viktor Gyoekeres , who this time acted as the creator. He laid the ball off to Bukayo Saka , and the England international clinical finish with his left foot doubled the lead. Fulham appeared shell-shocked, and their defensive woes were compounded in stoppage time. In the 45+4th minute, Leandro Trossard delivered a precise cross that found Viktor Gyoekeres , who headed home his second of the afternoon to put Arsenal in a commanding position heading into the break. Tactical Adjustments and Fulham's Response The second half began with Mikel Arteta opting for caution, replacing Bukayo Saka with Noni Madueke . Fulham showed signs of life early in the period, winning a series of corners. Timothy Castagne saw a goal-bound header blocked during a frantic 50th-minute spell where Harry Wilson and Harrison Reed peppered the box with deliveries. However, David Raya and his defense held firm despite a few nervous moments at the back. As the hour mark passed, both managers turned to their benches to refresh their squads. Arsenal introduced Martin Zubimendi and Gabriel Jesus , while Fulham brought on Oscar Bobb and Rodrigo Muniz . The game became somewhat fragmented as a result of the changes and a series of offside calls against Gabriel Jesus and Ben White , which prevented the Gunners from extending their lead further. Closing Stages and Final Whistle The final ten minutes saw Arsenal manage the game professionally, maintaining 54% of the possession. Max Dowman , having come on for Eberechi Eze , had a late chance to add a fourth, but his effort whistled wide of the post. Fulham continued to search for a consolation goal, with Tom Cairney and Rodrigo Muniz trying to spark an attack, but a defensive blunder by Gabriel in the 92nd minute went unpunished as Cristhian Mosquera arrived to clear the danger. The referee brought an end to the contest after four minutes of added time, confirming a comprehensive performance for the North London side. While Fulham showed flashes of resilience in the second period, the clinical nature of Arsenal's first-half display proved to be the difference in this Premier League encounter. With both managers known for their meticulous preparation, the stage was set for a match where discipline and clinical execution would prove to be the ultimate currency. A Cagey Opening in Madrid The opening exchanges reflected the high stakes of the competition, with both Atletico Madrid and Arsenal looking to find their footing without overcommitting. The visitors survived an early scare in the first minute when Piero Hincapie committed a defensive blunder, though the hosts were unable to punish the lapse. As the half progressed, the English side began to find more joy in the final third. Noni Madueke was particularly lively, cutting inside in the 30th minute to unleash a stinging effort from the edge of the box that whistled just wide of the upright, serving as a stern warning to the Atletico backline. Gyoekeres Breaks the Deadlock The tension finally broke just before the interval through a moment of controversy and clinical finishing. In the 43rd minute, Viktor Gyoekeres was bundled over in the area by David Hancko , prompting the referee to immediately point to the penalty spot. A lengthy VAR review followed, testing the nerves of both sets of players, but the original decision stood. Viktor Gyoekeres took responsibility, striking the ball with enough venom that despite Jan Oblak getting a strong hand to the shot, he could not prevent it from hitting the back of the net. The goal gave Arsenal a narrow lead and left the Metropolitano silenced as the teams headed into the tunnel. Atletico Strike Back from the Spot Diego Simeone looked to change the game's momentum at the start of the second half, introducing Robin Le Normand for Giuliano Simeone . The tactical shift bore fruit in the 54th minute when a corner from Antoine Griezmann led to a handball by Ben White in a crowded penalty area. After another trip to the pitchside monitor, the referee awarded a penalty to the hosts. Julian Alvarez stepped up for Atletico Madrid and showed remarkable composure, slotting his right-footed effort past David Raya , who opted to stay central. The equalizer breathed new life into the stadium, prompting Mikel Arteta to respond with a triple substitution that saw Bukayo Saka , Gabriel Jesus , and Leandro Trossard enter the fray. Late VAR Twist and Missed Opportunities The drama reached a crescendo in the 78th minute when Arsenal thought they had earned a golden opportunity to reclaim the lead. Eberechi Eze , who had replaced Martin Odegaard earlier in the half, was judged to have been fouled by David Hancko . The Atletico defender was cautioned for his vociferous protests, but his frustration turned to relief minutes later. Following a VAR intervention, the referee overturned the penalty decision, much to the frustration of the Arsenal bench. In the final minutes of stoppage time, both sides searched for a winner. Nahuel Molina forced a save from David Raya with a shot from distance, while Leandro Trossard missed a glaring opportunity for the visitors after miskicking from a promising position inside the box. Despite the late pressure, neither side could find the decisive blow, leaving the match to end in a fiercely contested draw that keeps the balance of power perfectly poised.

Despite late attempts from Martin Zubimendi and Desiré Doué , the deadlock could not be broken, leading the match into a penalty shootout. In the final act of the drama, Paris Saint-Germain displayed superior composure from twelve yards.
